contract: Provider-neutral text-model interface: request (ordered text messages, tools, tool_choice, output schema, max output tokens, stop sequences, optional sampling, reasoning level, cache hint, declared provider options, dispatch identity, deadline) admitted from a core/effect declaration with local refusals before any intent; one provider call per dispatch through the delivery/effect-intent owner; outcomes completed{content, tool_proposals, structured, finish, usage, provenance} | refused{credentials_unavailable | invalid_request | unsupported_feature | too_large | authentication_failed | permission_denied | throttled | overloaded | not_found} | unknown{timeout | transport | malformed_response | provider_error}; throttled and overloaded are failed/dispatched/retryable and not redispatched by default (Contract amendment 1); only credentials_unavailable is attested no-send and retried under delivery/retry-timeout; tool proposals are inert data, malformed ones marked; structured output validated; volatile result sink; provider behaviour and conformance kit.
limits: No automatic retry of a provider-reported throttle or overload: a caller retries only with its own ground, for example a new logical request reference accepting that the first request may have been processed.
The result sink is volatile local delivery: no durable retention, replay, recovery delivery or exactly-once delivery; after a restart only the settled status remains.
The completion seal is process-local integrity of the Adapter's own result, not provider authentication.
Streaming, batch, vision and document input, provider-executed tools, routing, fallback, pricing, metering, conversation storage and agent loops are not supplied.
Tenants that share one provider credential share that provider's prompt cache; the cache-hint tenant rule cannot partition it.
Finite scenarios with a scripted test provider and a volatile store; no proof is claimed.

grounding.claim: Pinned Cure compilation type-checks the finite failure-tag to Contract-outcome and delivery-result decision; the static Binding table is checked equal to it at construction. Not a proof of provider behaviour.

Listed scenarios with a scripted test provider and the volatile Memory store: completed call path with content only through the sink; local refusals before intent, credential and call; provider options; retries (credentials_unavailable retried, throttled and overloaded unresolved and not redispatched, unknown never, also under a redispatch_idempotent policy); second dispatch refused and same key on re-admission; classification table against Cure; sink failures; tool proposal and structured-output checks; request codec; configuration and redaction; a source audit of this Piece's own listed files showing no reference to req_llm, llm_db, Plug, Req.Test or the Anthropic provider module (the interface loads no provider dependency). Finite scenarios, not proofs.
jsv 0.27.0 JSON Schema draft 2020-12 build and validate without remote resolution, as exercised in the listed scenarios.
Relies on pinned compilation and nullary-sum erasure; not a local proof of the compiler.

Provider Pieces implement the behaviour truthfully: one HTTP exchange per call, failure tags chosen from documented statuses, absent usage fields reported :unknown; the host keeps the credential Need truthful; a provider's documented 'rejected before generation' meaning of a throttle or overload is not relied on.

telemetry.contract: No Elzoo event; provider libraries may emit their own events to consumer-installed handlers. Own events through runtime/telemetry: future task when a consumer needs them. Not inherited: runtime/telemetry is not a dependency.

config.contract: Construction-time binding (provider account entering the intent key), tenant, provider and its construction term, credential Need, model allowlist, request-byte bound, output-token cap, receive timeout and result sink; per-request deadline from the declaration; no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: Call-scoped: dispatch, rearm and expiry are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control; a deadline cannot erase a dispatched call, which is reported unknown.
